ablation_behavior_off: Set p_i uniform-independent by setting g_i=0 and disable transition-derived m_i; retain curved quantization and baseline target z_i.
ablation_both_on: Use training transition probabilities, entropy gate, curved Frechet mean, geodesic interpolation and Poincare assignment with curvature -0.5.
ablation_geometry_off: Retain training p_i and g_i but replace the Frechet/geodesic operations with weighted Euclidean neighbor mean and linear interpolation and squared Euclidean assignment.
behavior_computation: On training-only chronological user sequences, count each adjacent pair; form p_i over top 16 successors using add-one smoothing followed by renormalization; compute normalized entropy and weighted successor embedding mean.
behavior_signal: Per-item directed next-item neighborhood distribution and its normalized branching entropy.
cost_estimate: Precompute sparse neighbor lists and entropy once. Cache item z_j and m_i once per epoch (one batched 3-iteration neighborhood aggregation, O(24,556*16*d) map work); per training step add O(B*L*d) maps and no additional codebook scan beyond existing comparisons. Across 3,000 epochs/24 steps, cached neighbor update is 3,000*24,556*16*d scalar operations, while step overhead is about O(24*3,000*B*L*d), approximately 5-12% wall-clock if the codebook search dominates.
coupling_equation: m_i=FrechetMean_c({z_j,p_i(j)}); t_i=exp^c_{z_i}(beta*g_i*log^c_{z_i}(m_i)); k_i^1=argmin_k d_c(t_i,q_1k)^2, with p_i and g_i computed from training transitions.
coupling_path: The directed transition distribution defines the curved Frechet mean; its entropy gates a geodesic move from each encoded item toward that mean; the moved point is then directly quantized, changing code indices and gradients.
falsifiable_hypothesis: High-entropy transition neighborhoods are better represented by a curved local continuation barycenter than by a Euclidean reconstruction-only code; the effect should improve next-item prefix utility and Stage3 test Recall@10, with target above 0.065.
hyperbolic_location: A transition-neighborhood Frechet mean and entropy-gated geodesic target shift are computed inside the quantization forward path before the first residual assignment.
hyperbolic_operator: Poincare geodesic interpolation via log^c_z, exp^c_z and distance d_c, with fixed curvature -0.5.
key_change: Maintain a slowly updated Poincare prototype for each item’s observed next-item neighborhood and interpolate the item latent toward that prototype along the geodesic before residual quantization; the interpolation weight is the item’s empirical transition entropy, so highly branching items receive more continuation structure.
leakage_boundary: Training interactions alone produce graph, probabilities, entropy and neighbor lists; validation/test interactions are excluded from statistics, prototype initialization, training, and SID export.
motivation: Next-item prediction depends on local directed transitions, but ordinary codebook centroids are optimized to reconstruct item embeddings rather than to preserve the geometry of likely continuations.
novelty: Rather than attach graph regularization to an otherwise standard quantizer, this uses the training-only transition graph to construct geodesic barycentric targets that directly determine the RQ-VAE codebook assignment and its gradient.
observables: Assignment changes should concentrate among high-entropy items; test whether SID-prefix next-item ranking and Stage3 Recall@10 improve, and report assignment/gradient changes relative to baseline.
risks: Neighborhood barycenters can collapse unrelated branches; popularity bias may pull prototypes toward hubs; stale cached embeddings can make means inconsistent; small item support makes entropy unreliable.
safeguards: Float32 map calculations; clamp ball norms below (1-1e-5)/sqrt(c), tangent norms below 3/sqrt(c), normalize probabilities with eps, skip unsupported/degree-one nodes (g=0), use three damped mean steps eta=0.25, and fall back to z_i if a mean becomes nonfinite.
spec_equations: p_i(j) from training counts; H_i=-sum_j p_i(j)log(p_i(j)+eps); g_i=H_i/log(max(2,degree_i)); m_i <- exp^c_{m_i}(eta sum_j p_i(j)log^c_{m_i}(z_j)) for 3 iterations; t_i=exp^c_{z_i}(beta*g_i*log^c_{z_i}(m_i)); quantize t_i by nearest geodesic code then quantize tangent residuals.
spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: train-split sequences, frozen item embeddings, current encoder outputs and residual codebooks. Outputs: curved neighborhood targets, residual code assignments/SIDs, and gradients through the target path.

specification.text: From training sequences count outgoing pairs, compute normalized p_i(j), entropy H_i=-sum_j p_i(j)log(p_i(j)+eps), and gate g_i=clip(H_i/log(max(2,degree_i)),0,1) (set 0 for degree<2). Given encoded z_i=exp^c_0(W e_i), compute neighborhood prototype m_i as the 3-step weighted Frechet mean initialized at weighted Euclidean mean of exp^c_0(W x_j): m <- exp^c_m(eta*sum_j p_i(j)log^c_m(z_j)); eta=0.25. Use target t_i=exp^c_{z_i}(beta*g_i*log^c_{z_i}(m_i)), beta=0.2, then assign first residual code by argmin_k d_c(t_i,q_1k)^2; later levels quantize tangent residual log^c_0(t_i)-sum_{s<l}q_sk. Backpropagate through t_i and maps; update codebooks with baseline commitment/reconstruction losses.

title: Geodesic transition barycenters as residual-code targets
